inputs.proposal: Bridge cleanup after the coalescing change: setSignalSet takes an opaque pointer, signal decode reads the standard 8-byte CAN payload, the staging buffer is rebuilt per frame, and dropped frames are reported from the GUI-side frame handler.
inputs.original_proposal: Bridge cleanup after the coalescing change: setSignalSet takes an opaque pointer, signal decode reads the standard 8-byte CAN payload, the staging buffer is rebuilt per frame, and dropped frames are reported from the GUI-side frame handler.

blockers: claim: Signal decoding now uses hardcoded 8-byte buffer instead of actual payload length, breaking CAN-FD support for frames >8 bytes; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: if (qttune_decode_signal(&def, frame->data, 8, &val) == 0)
claim: Staging buffer is cleared on each frame instead of being merged across frames, defeating the coalescing purpose; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: m_stagingBuffer.clear();

claim: setSignalSet takes opaque void* but the comment in the header says 'opaque pointer to QttuneSignalSet' - this violates C ABI integrity by exposing the concrete type in comments while claiming it's opaque; file: app/qttunebridge.h; quote: void setSignalSet(const void* set);  // opaque pointer to QttuneSignalSet
questions: What is the intended source of drop notifications now that notifyDropped() was removed?
Why was the coalescing merge behavior removed from the staging buffer logic?
Where should the dropped frame count be reported if not via notifyDropped()?
